pages.name: Music in the room the TV is in

artboards.title: Today: music playing in the TV's room
A: what plays here, first in the room
B: the resting TV shows the record

annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS

Step 4 of the living room (20 November 2026) was music to the TV's soundbar. In our living room the HomePods are the speakers, so the hub never plays through the TV: the music stays on the room's own speakers (design/music/, A), and the TV becomes the screen for it -- what is playing, and the remote to work it.

THE SAME IN BOTH

Nothing new is played: the speakers in the TV's room play, and choosing what is still the music pane (design/music/, A with C's sentences), opened with Hold OK.

Only when something plays in the TV's own room; music in the kitchen is the kitchen's.

Read from the sofa: nothing under 22px.

A: WHAT PLAYS HERE, FIRST IN THE ROOM

While music plays in the room, a row of its own leads the TV's home: the record, where it plays and how loud, Next, and Other rooms. OK pauses, Up and Down are the volume.

FOR: one press from the sofa, where the highlight already starts.

AGAINST: changes nothing at rest, and resting is when a TV with music on mostly sits.

B: THE RESTING TV SHOWS THE RECORD

While music plays in the room and the TV rests, the record fills it, with the time in a corner. OK raises the band (the living room's, OverC) with Pause, Next and the volume.

FOR: the TV looks like what the room is doing, which is playing music.

AGAINST: awake, the speaker is still the last card in its row.

Try it: Enter, then Escape.

DECIDED 20 NOVEMBER 2026

Both: A while the TV is awake, B while it rests. A paused record still leads the awake room, so it can be started again from the sofa; at rest only music that plays takes the screen.
